topic: man held with turtles at dhaka airport
headline_marked: 1,163 turtles seized: [[Man held with 1,163 turtles]] at Dhaka airport
headline: 1,163 turtles seized: Man held with 1,163 turtles at Dhaka airport
summary: A 57-year-old man from Tangail was detained while attempting to smuggle native Kori Kaitta turtles to Malaysia.
details: Law-enforcing agencies and the Wildlife Crime Control Unit (WCCU) detained a man at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport in Dhaka on Saturday night.
The detainee, identified as Md Shahidul Islam, 57, was a passenger on a Batik Air flight bound for Malaysia.
A search of his luggage revealed 1,163 live "Kori Kaitta" turtles, which were seized by the authorities.
During interrogation, the suspect claimed he was paid to transport the luggage and could not provide further information.
Wildlife Inspector Asim Mallick stated that authorities suspect a larger smuggling ring is operating behind the operation.
A case has been filed against the suspect at Shahjalal International Airport Police Station for violating the Wildlife (Conservation and Security) Act.
The rescued turtles will be released into their natural habitat after receiving initial medical care.
caption:
1,163 live turtles hidden in luggage! A man was caught attempting to smuggle them from Dhaka to Malaysia.

Law-enforcing agencies and the Wildlife Crime Control Unit (WCCU) detained a man at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport in Dhaka on Saturday night.

The detainee, identified as Md Shahidul Islam, 57, was a passenger on a Batik Air flight bound for Malaysia.

A search of his luggage revealed 1,163 live "Kori Kaitta" turtles, which were seized by the authorities.

During interrogation, the suspect claimed he was paid to transport the luggage and could not provide further information.

Wildlife Inspector Asim Mallick stated that authorities suspect a larger smuggling ring is operating behind the operation.

A case has been filed against the suspect at Shahjalal International Airport Police Station for violating the Wildlife (Conservation and Security) Act.

The rescued turtles will be released into their natural habitat after receiving initial medical care.
